m:altstadt: Free to walk, at any hour. In Austria shops are closed on Sundays and public holidays: cafés, restaurants and museums stay open. During the Christmas markets (from 20 November) the centre is much more crowded.
m:festung: 2026 prices (the fortress's official website, valid from 1 February): Panorama Ticket with funicular €12.80, Festungscard «Basic» €15.50, «All Inclusive» €19.20; walking up, prices are lower (€10.10, €12.00 and €14.50). Hours from October to December: 9:30am–5pm. The funicular (€4 one way, €6.30 return) is closed for maintenance from 9 to 13 November 2026 and from 11 January to 14 March 2027: you can still reach the fortress on foot.
m:dom: The DomQuartier is open every day except Tuesday, from 10am to 5pm (last entry an hour before; closed on 24 December). The Residenzgalerie is closed until autumn 2027 and since 17 August 2026 the Dombogen terrace can only be reached through the Cathedral Museum. I couldn't read the ticket price on the official website: to be confirmed on domquartier.at. Check the cathedral's hours on the spot, because the church closes during services.
m:geburtshaus: Open every day from 9am to 5:30pm (from a 2022 guide, hours to be confirmed on the Mozarteum Foundation website). I couldn't find the price of a Birthplace-only ticket in the official 2026 sources: about €15, to be confirmed. The combined ticket with the Mozart Residence costs €23 (ticket sales website, 2026). It isn't high season: you can usually get in without booking.
m:wohnhaus: Open every day from 9am to 5:30pm, last entry 30 minutes before closing; on 24 December from 9am to 1pm and on 1 January from noon (ticket sales website, 2026). Full ticket €15, combined ticket with the Birthplace €23. It also gives access to the concert hall.
m:mirabell: The garden is free and open every day from 6am. The palace is normally open from 8am to 6pm and the Marble Hall (Marmorsaal) has limited hours during the week (Mon, Wed, Thu 8am–4pm; Tue and Fri 1–4pm): data from a 2022 guide, to be confirmed.
m:monchsberg: The path is free. The lift (Mönchsbergaufzug) has a paid ticket, whose price and hours I couldn't check on the official website: to be confirmed. In ice or snow some paths are slippery.
m:hellbrunn: Open every day from 28 March to 1 November 2026 (official website), from October 9:30am to 5:30pm with last entry at 4:30pm; ticket for palace and trick fountains €16.50 (official website). After 1 November there are no visits to the palace and trick fountains until spring 2027 (dates to be confirmed); the gardens stay open from 6:30am to 9pm, and from 20 November to 24 December there's the Christmas market. Reach it by bus from the centre or on foot in about 45 minutes.
m:museum: Hours and price from an older guide (2022): open Tuesday to Sunday from 9am to 5pm, closed on Mondays; full price about €9. The museum has changed exhibitions since then: to be confirmed on the official website before going.
m:stpeter: The church and cemetery are free to visit during the day, but I didn't read the exact winter hours on the official website: to be confirmed on the spot. The catacombs have a separate ticket (price to be confirmed). The Stiftskeller restaurant is in the same complex.
vd:tomaselli: Salzburg's historic café, open since 1705 on the Alter Markt: stuccoed rooms, waiters with trays of cakes to choose from, and a Melange with the classic apple strudel.
vp:tomaselli: A coffee with a slice of cake is around €9–12 (menu not seen). Hours from a guide: other sources give a later evening closing (7pm or 9pm), to be confirmed.
vd:fuerst: The pâtisserie where in 1890 Paul Fürst invented the Mozartkugel, the ball of pistachio, marzipan and dark chocolate. Have breakfast with a slice of cake or buy a box to take home.
vp:fuerst: A Mozartkugel costs about €1.50–2 each; a coffee with a cake is around €8–11 (menu not seen). Hours from a guide: other sources give longer opening, to be confirmed.
vd:bazar: A literary café since 1909 on the right bank of the Salzach, with a terrace on the river and the fortress opposite. Have a Melange with Milchrahmstrudel, or a sandwich or an omelette for lunch.
vp:bazar: A coffee with a cake is around €8–11 and a light dish around €10–14 (menu not seen). Cash only (from a guide). Some sources say it's also open on Sundays: to be confirmed.
vd:ratio: A small roastery on the Linzergasse, near the Kapuzinerberg: specialty coffee (filter, flat white), a few cakes and a light snack, with some outdoor tables.
vp:ratio: A coffee is around €3.50–5 and a slice of cake €4–6 (menu not seen). Hours from a guide, to be confirmed.
vd:alchemie: A specialty café on the Rudolfskai riverside, with more than ten coffees of different origins and homemade cakes, in a cosy, quiet setting.
vp:alchemie: A coffee is around €3.50–5 and a cake €4–6 (menu not seen). Hours from a guide: at weekends it opens at about 9am, to be confirmed.
vd:grad: A family roastery in the Kaiviertel, next to the Festspielhaus: espresso and filter coffee, a small menu of dishes and cakes for a quiet break after the old town.
vp:grad: A coffee is around €3.50–5, a light dish €9–13 (menu not seen). Closed on Mondays according to a guide, to be confirmed.
vd:braustubl: Austria's largest monastery brewery: beer is poured from wooden barrels into stone mugs, you get food from the stalls in the passage (sausages, roast pork, pretzels) and sit in the halls or the chestnut-shaded garden. First pay for the mug at the till and take it with the receipt to the tap.
vp:braustubl: Half a litre of beer costs about €5–6; a traditional dish is around €10–15 (menu not seen). I have the hours from undated sources (it opens in the afternoon): to be confirmed on the website.
vd:stiftskeller: A restaurant inside St Peter's Abbey that bills itself as one of Europe's oldest, with vaulted rooms and a courtyard: Salzburg cooking with dishes like Tafelspitz (boiled beef) and Nockerl, the sweet meringue that's the city's emblem.
vp:stiftskeller: A main course is around €18–28 (menu not seen). It's a bit pricier than the other places on the list. Hours from undated sources: to be confirmed, and best to book in the evening.
cd:domquartier: A route through the Residenz, the Cathedral and the abbey, with the art gallery and the rooftops.
cd:catacombe: Caves dug into the rock of the Mönchsberg, used by early Christians.
cd:untersberg: A cable car to the summit, with views of the Alps and the city.
cx:untersberg: It's in Grödig, about 8 km from the centre.
cd:salzbergwerk: A mine with wooden slides and an underground lake.
cx:salzbergwerk: It's in Hallein, about 15 km from Salzburg.
cd:salzachcruise: Fifty minutes on the river between the old town and the palaces.
cd:hausnatur: A science museum with aquariums, reptiles and a space section.
cd:soundofmusic: By coach to the film's locations: Mirabell, Leopoldskron Palace and the lakes.
